# Data input & processing and initialization of CellChat object
```{r input_data}
ptm = Sys.time()
getwd()
# Prepare required input data for CellChat analysis
seurat_object_all <- readRDS(params$seurat_integrated)
seurat_object_Macro <- readRDS(params$seurat_Macro)
seurat_object_EC <- readRDS(params$seurat_EC)
seurat_object_ASPC <- readRDS(params$seurat_ASPC)

table(seurat_object_all$renamed_cluster)
table(seurat_object_Macro$sub_cluster)
table(seurat_object_EC$sub_cluster)
table(seurat_object_ASPC$sub_cluster)

colnames(seurat_object_all@meta.data)
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster <- NA

length(intersect(Cells(seurat_object_Macro), Cells(seurat_object_all)))
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[Cells(seurat_object_Macro)] <- seurat_object_Macro$sub_cluster
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[Cells(seurat_object_EC)] <- seurat_object_EC$sub_cluster
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[Cells(seurat_object_ASPC)] <- seurat_object_ASPC$sub_cluster
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[seurat_object_all$sub_cluster == "1"] <- "Areg"
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[seurat_object_all$sub_cluster == "2"] <- "FAP"
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[seurat_object_all$sub_cluster == "3"] <- "ASC"
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[seurat_object_all$sub_cluster == "4"] <- "PreA"
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[seurat_object_all$sub_cluster == "5"] <- "RMP"
table(seurat_object_all$sub_cluster)

# 替换sub_cluster列中NA值为renamed_cluster列中的相应值
seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[is.na(seurat_object_all$sub_cluster)] <- seurat_object_all$renamed_cluster[is.na(seurat_object_all$sub_cluster)]
table(seurat_object_all$sub_cluster)
unique(seurat_object_all$sub_cluster)

# seurat_object_all$sub_cluster[seurat_object_all$sub_cluster == "ASPC"] <- NA

Idents(seurat_object_all) <- "sub_cluster"
cells_to_remove <- WhichCells(seurat_object_all, idents = "ASPC")
seurat_object_all <- subset(seurat_object_all, cells = cells_to_remove, invert = TRUE)
cells_to_remove <- WhichCells(seurat_object_all, idents = "Endothelial Cell")
seurat_object_all <- subset(seurat_object_all, cells = cells_to_remove, invert = TRUE)

# Chow dataset
seurat_object_Chow <- subset(seurat_object_all, subset = sample == "Chow")
# HFSC dataset
seurat_object_HFSC <- subset(seurat_object_all, subset = sample == "HFSC")
seurat_object_Chow
seurat_object_HFSC
```

# **Chow group
```{r path_chow}
data_dir_chow <- file.path(params$output_dir, "data/chow/", Sys.Date())
results_dir_chow <- file.path(params$output_dir, "results/chow/", Sys.Date())

invisible(mapply(
  FUN = dir.create,
  list(data_dir_chow, results_dir_chow),
  MoreArgs = list(recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
))
```

```{r Chow_input}
data.input <- seurat_object_Chow@assays$RNA$counts
dim(data.input)
meta = seurat_object_Chow@meta.data
meta = meta[colnames(data.input),]
meta = data.frame(row.names = rownames(meta), celltype = meta$sub_cluster)

# Create a CellChat object
cellchat_Chow <- createCellChat(object = data.input, meta = meta, group.by = "celltype")
cellchat_Chow@meta$samples <- "vWAT"

#cellchat <- setIdent(cellchat, ident.use = "labels") # set "labels" as default cell identity
levels(cellchat_Chow@idents) # show factor levels of the cell labels
groupSize <- as.numeric(table(cellchat_Chow@idents)) # number of cells in each cell group

# Set the ligand-receptor interaction database
CellChatDB <- CellChatDB.mouse
showDatabaseCategory(CellChatDB)
# Show the structure of the database
dplyr::glimpse(CellChatDB$interaction)
# use a subset of CellChatDB for cell-cell communication analysis
CellChatDB.use <- subsetDB(CellChatDB, search = "Secreted Signaling", key = "annotation") # use Secreted Signaling, the other three are `Cell-Cell Contact`,`ECM-Receptor`, `Non-protein Signaling`.
cellchat_Chow@DB <- CellChatDB.use

# Preprocessing the expression data for cell-cell communication analysis
cellchat_Chow <- subsetData(cellchat_Chow) # This step is necessary even if using the whole database
future::plan("multisession", workers = 4) # do parallel
cellchat_Chow <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat_Chow)
cellchat_Chow <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat_Chow)
cellchat_Chow@data

dim(data.input)
length(labels)
execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
print(as.numeric(execution.time, units = "secs"))
```
## I. Inference of CCC network
```{r CCC_network}
# Compute the communication probability and infer cellular communication network
ptm = Sys.time()

cellchat_Chow <- computeCommunProb(cellchat_Chow, type = "triMean")
cellchat_Chow <- filterCommunication(cellchat_Chow, min.cells = 10)

# Extract the inferred cellular communication network as a data frame
df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_Chow) # returns a data frame consisting of all the inferred cell-cell communications at the level of ligands/receptors. Set slot.name = "netP" to access the the inferred communications at the level of signaling pathways
# df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_Chow, sources.use = c(1,2), targets.use = c(4,5)) # gives the inferred cell-cell communications sending from cell groups 1 and 2 to cell groups 4 and 5.
# df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_Chow, signaling = c("WNT", "TGFb")) # gives the inferred cell-cell communications mediated by signaling WNT and TGFb.

# Infer the cell-cell communication at a signaling pathway level
cellchat_Chow <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat_Chow)

# Calculate the aggregated cell-cell communication network
cellchat_Chow <- aggregateNet(cellchat_Chow)
execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
print(as.numeric(execution.time, units = "secs"))

ptm = Sys.time()
groupSize <- as.numeric(table(cellchat_Chow@idents))

par(mfrow = c(1,2), xpd=TRUE)
#netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$count, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Number of interactions")
#netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$weight, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Interaction weights/strength")

getwd()
pdf(file.path(data_dir_chow, paste0("Number of interactions.pdf")), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$count, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Number of interactions")
dev.off()

pdf(file.path(data_dir_chow, paste0("Interaction weights and strength.pdf")), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_Chow@net$weight, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Interaction weights/strength")
dev.off()

mat <- cellchat_Chow@net$weight
plots_list <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(mat)) {
  mat2 <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(mat), ncol = ncol(mat), dimnames = dimnames(mat))
  mat2[i, ] <- mat[i, ]
  png(filename = sprintf('./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/%s_signaling.png',rownames(mat)[i]), width = 5, height = 5,units="in",res=500)
  p <- netVisual_circle(mat2, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, edge.weight.max = max(mat), title.name = rownames(mat)[i])
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  plots_list[[i]] <- p
}
```

## III: Systems analysis of cell-cell communication network
To facilitate the interpretation of the complex intercellular communication networks, CellChat quantitively measures networks through methods abstracted from graph theory, pattern recognition and manifold learning.
### Identify signaling roles (e.g., dominant senders, receivers) of cell groups as well as the major contributing signaling
```{r CCC_network}
ptm = Sys.time()
# (A) Compute and visualize the network centrality scores
pathways.show <- "CCL"
# Compute the network centrality scores
cellchat_Chow <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(cellchat_Chow, slot.name = "netP") # the slot 'netP' means the inferred intercellular communication network of signaling pathways
# Visualize the computed centrality scores using heatmap, allowing ready identification of major signaling roles of cell groups
png(sprintf(paste0("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/%s_centrality_scores",".png"),pathways.show),width = 6.5, height = 3, units = "in", res = 500)
netAnalysis_signalingRole_network(cellchat_Chow, signaling = pathways.show, width = 12, height = 3, font.size = 9, cluster.cols = T, cluster.rows = T)
dev.off()

pathways.show <- "COMPLEMENT"
cellchat_Chow <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(cellchat_Chow, slot.name = "netP") 
png("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/COMPLEMENT_centrality_scores.png", width = 6, height = 3, units = "in", res = 500)
netAnalysis_signalingRole_network(cellchat_Chow, signaling = pathways.show, width = 10, height = 3, font.size = 9,cluster.cols = T, cluster.rows = T)
dev.off()

gg1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow,title = "All signaling pathways", 
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow, signaling = "CCL", title = "CCL signaling pathway",
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg3 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_Chow, signaling = "COMPLEMENT", title = "COMPLEMENT signaling pathway",
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg1 + gg2 + gg3
ggsave("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter_3.pdf", width = 12, height = 4)

pathways.show <- c("CCL","COMPLEMENT","SEMA3","ANGPTL","MIF","FGF","CXCL","PDGF","TGFb","VEGF","ADIPONECTIN","RESISTIN","SPP1","ncWNT","WNT","CHEMERIN","GALECTIN","IGF","BMP","ANGPT")
cell.order <- c("Areg", "ASC", "FAP", "PreA", "RMP", "VEC", 
                "REC", "MesEC", "MbEC", "LEC", "IREC", 
                "RM", "PVM", "PLAM", "NPVM", "CEM1", "CEM2", 
                "Mesothelial Cell", "Neutrophil", "Dendritic Cell", 
                "T Cell", "B Cell", "Smooth Muscle Cell")

pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/outgoing_incoming_rank.pdf", width = 10, height = 8) # width = 7,height = 8
ht1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing", signaling = pathways.show, width = 8,height = 6)
ht2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming", signaling = pathways.show, width = 8, height = 6)
ht1 + ht2
dev.off()
```

### Identify global communication patterns to explore how multiple cell types and signaling pathways coordinate together
In addition to exploring detailed communications for individual pathways, an important question is how multiple cell groups and signaling pathways coordinate to function. CellChat employs a pattern recognition method to identify the global communication patterns.
```{r pattern}
# (A) Identify and visualize outgoing communication pattern of secreting cells
library(NMF)
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/patterns_selectK.pdf",width = 6, height = 4)
selectK(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing") # We run selectK to infer the number of patterns.
dev.off()
#Both Cophenetic and Silhouette values begin to drop suddenly when the number of outgoing patterns is 4.
nPatterns = 3
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/patterns_outgoing.pdf", width = 8, height = 12)
cellchat_Chow <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "outgoing", k = nPatterns, width = 4, height = 12)
dev.off()

# (B) Identify and visualize incoming communication pattern of target cells
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/patterns_selectK_incoming.pdf",width = 6, height = 4)
selectK(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming") # We run selectK to infer the number of patterns.
dev.off()
nPatterns = 4
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/chow/2024-09-24/patterns_incoming.pdf",width = 8, height = 12)
cellchat_Chow <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(cellchat_Chow, pattern = "incoming", k = nPatterns,width = 4, height = 12)
dev.off()
```

```{r HFSC_input}
future::plan("multisession", workers = 4) # do parallel
cellchat_HFSC <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat_HFSC)
cellchat_HFSC <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat_HFSC)
cellchat_HFSC@data

dim(data.input)

execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
```

## I. Inference of cell-cell communication network
```{r CCC_network}
# Compute the communication probability and infer cellular communication network
ptm = Sys.time()

cellchat_HFSC <- computeCommunProb(cellchat_HFSC, type = "triMean")
cellchat_HFSC <- filterCommunication(cellchat_HFSC, min.cells = 10)

# Extract the inferred cellular communication network as a data frame
df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_HFSC) # returns a data frame consisting of all the inferred cell-cell communications at the level of ligands/receptors. Set slot.name = "netP" to access the the inferred communications at the level of signaling pathways
# df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_HFSC, sources.use = c(1,2), targets.use = c(4,5)) # gives the inferred cell-cell communications sending from cell groups 1 and 2 to cell groups 4 and 5.
# df.net <- subsetCommunication(cellchat_HFSC, signaling = c("WNT", "TGFb")) # gives the inferred cell-cell communications mediated by signaling WNT and TGFb.

# Infer the cell-cell communication at a signaling pathway level
cellchat_HFSC <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat_HFSC)

# Calculate the aggregated cell-cell communication network
cellchat_HFSC <- aggregateNet(cellchat_HFSC)
execution.time = Sys.time() - ptm
print(as.numeric(execution.time, units = "secs"))

ptm = Sys.time()
groupSize <- as.numeric(table(cellchat_HFSC@idents))

par(mfrow = c(1,2), xpd=TRUE)
#netVisual_circle(cellchat_HFSC@net$count, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Number of interactions")
#netVisual_circle(cellchat_HFSC@net$weight, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Interaction weights/strength")

pdf(file.path(data_dir_hfsc, paste0("Number of interactions.pdf")), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_HFSC@net$count, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Number of interactions")
dev.off()

pdf(file.path(data_dir_hfsc, paste0("Interaction weights and strength.pdf")), width = 5, height = 6)
netVisual_circle(cellchat_HFSC@net$weight, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, label.edge= F, title.name = "Interaction weights/strength")
dev.off()

mat <- cellchat_HFSC@net$weight
plots_list <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(mat)) {
  mat2 <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(mat), ncol = ncol(mat), dimnames = dimnames(mat))
  mat2[i, ] <- mat[i, ]
  png(filename = sprintf('./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/%s_signaling.png',rownames(mat)[i]), width = 5, height = 5,units="in",res=500)
  p <- netVisual_circle(mat2, vertex.weight = groupSize, weight.scale = T, edge.weight.max = max(mat), title.name = rownames(mat)[i])
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  plots_list[[i]] <- p
}
```

## III: Systems analysis of cell-cell communication network
To facilitate the interpretation of the complex intercellular communication networks, CellChat quantitively measures networks through methods abstracted from graph theory, pattern recognition and manifold learning.
### Identify signaling roles (e.g., dominant senders, receivers) of cell groups as well as the major contributing signaling
```{r CCC_network}
ptm = Sys.time()
# (A) Compute and visualize the network centrality scores
cellchat_HFSC <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(cellchat_HFSC, slot.name = "netP") # the slot 'netP' means the 

pathways.show <- "TGFb"
png(sprintf(paste0("./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/%s_centrality_scores.png"),pathways.show), 
    width = 6.5, height = 3, units = "in", res = 500)
netAnalysis_signalingRole_network(cellchat_HFSC, signaling = pathways.show, 
                                  width = 12, height = 2.5, font.size = 10,
                                  cluster.cols = T, cluster.rows = T)
dev.off()


gg1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_HFSC,title = "All signaling pathways", 
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_HFSC, signaling = "COMPLEMENT", title = "COMPLEMENT signaling pathway",
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg3 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(cellchat_HFSC, signaling = "ANGPTL", title = "ANGPTL signaling pathway",
                                         label.size = 3, dot.alpha = 0.5)
gg1 + gg2 + gg3
ggsave("./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter_3.pdf", width = 12, height = 4)

pathways.show <- c("COMPLEMENT","MIF","ANGPTL","SEMA3","GALECTIN","CCL","TGFb","CXCL","CSF","PDGF",
                   "VEGF","FGF","SPP1","BMP","ANGPT","ncWNT","EGF","TNF","TWEAK","WNT")

pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/outgoing_incoming_rank.pdf", width = 10, height = 8) # width = 7,height = 8
ht1 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_HFSC, pattern = "outgoing", signaling = pathways.show, width = 8,height = 6)
ht2 <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_heatmap(cellchat_HFSC, pattern = "incoming", signaling = pathways.show, width = 8,height = 6)
ht1 + ht2
dev.off()

```

### Identify global communication patterns to explore how multiple cell types and signaling pathways coordinate together
In addition to exploring detailed communications for individual pathways, an important question is how multiple cell groups and signaling pathways coordinate to function. CellChat employs a pattern recognition method to identify the global communication patterns.
```{r pattern}
# (A) Identify and visualize outgoing communication pattern of secreting cells
library(NMF)
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/patterns_selectK.pdf",width = 6, height = 4)
selectK(cellchat_HFSC, pattern = "outgoing") # We run selectK to infer the number of patterns.
dev.off()
#Both Cophenetic and Silhouette values begin to drop suddenly when the number of outgoing patterns is 4.
nPatterns = 2
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/patterns_outgoing.pdf", width = 8, height = 12)
cellchat_HFSC <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(cellchat_HFSC, pattern = "outgoing", k = nPatterns, width = 4, height = 12)
dev.off()

# (B) Identify and visualize incoming communication pattern of target cells
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/patterns_selectK_incoming.pdf",width = 6, height = 4)
selectK(cellchat_HFSC, pattern = "incoming") # We run selectK to infer the number of patterns.
dev.off()
nPatterns = 3
pdf("./CCC_Subcluster/results/hfsc/2024-10-09/patterns_incoming.pdf",width = 8, height = 12)
cellchat_HFSC <- identifyCommunicationPatterns(cellchat_HFSC, pattern = "incoming", k = nPatterns,width = 4, height = 12)
dev.off()
```
